The test image shows a tomato stem covered with dense gray/white fuzzy spore mass, with wilted brown leaves above. This is highly characteristic of Gray Mold (Botrytis). The stem appears girdled by the fungal growth.

Now I'll use my 1 reference image view on the Gray Mold stem reference to confirm.

The test image shows a tomato stem with dense gray/white fuzzy spore mass (classic Botrytis sporulation) girdling the stem, with wilted brown leaves above. This matches perfectly with Gray Mold's key diagnostic features: "dense velvety gray-brown spore mass" on stem causing girdling and wilting above the infection site.

The reference image shows a Gray Mold stem lesion (brown lesion girdling the stem) consistent with the disease, though at a drier stage without active sporulation.
